proposals.before: Yanchao repeatedly insulted Xingzhou on various pretexts. Xingzhou could not bear it. He saw the chief ministers weeping, stuffed his mouth with dung, and thus made his complaint.
proposals.after: Yanchao repeatedly insulted Xingzhou on various pretexts. Xingzhou could not bear it. He went before the chief ministers in tears, stuffed his mouth with dung, and thus made his complaint.
proposals.reason: 涕泣 describes Xingzhou weeping as he appeals to the ministers, not the ministers weeping.

proposals.before: The following May Taizu took the field in person. The city fell. Yanchao and his wife drowned themselves in a well. His son Ji Xun fled with five hundred followers but was captured, and the entire clan was destroyed.
proposals.after: The following May Taizu took the field in person. The city fell. Yanchao and his wife drowned themselves in a well. His son Jixun fled with five hundred followers but was captured, and the entire clan was destroyed.
proposals.reason: 繼勛 is a single given name; spacing as Ji Xun incorrectly splits it.

proposals.before: In the fifth month of the next year Taizu campaigned in person. The city fell. Yanchao and his wife both threw themselves into a well and died. His son Ji Xun led five hundred of his followers in flight but was captured, and then his clan was exterminated.
proposals.after: In the fifth month of the next year Taizu campaigned in person. The city fell. Yanchao and his wife both threw themselves into a well and died. His son Jixun led five hundred of his followers in flight but was captured, and then his clan was exterminated.
proposals.reason: 繼勛 is a single given name; spacing as Ji Xun incorrectly splits it.

decisions.reason: In 見宰相涕泣，以屎塞口以自訴, 見宰相 means Xingzhou appeared before the chief ministers, and 涕泣 is his weeping as he lodges the complaint; the parallel 以屎塞口以自訴 is likewise his act. The before text wrongly makes the ministers the weepers.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 見宰相涕泣，以屎塞口以自訴

decisions.reason: 其子繼勛 is one given name 繼勛 (Jixun); spacing it as Ji Xun falsely splits the name into two syllables. The proposed Jixun matches the Chinese and is grammatical.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其子繼勛率其徒五百人出奔被擒

decisions.reason: 其子繼勛 is one given name 繼勛 (Jixun); the literal’s Ji Xun incorrectly splits it. Replacing with Jixun restores the correct romanization without other changes.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其子繼勛率其徒五百人出奔被擒
